slides.title: Day 1 · The basics
slides.body: About every 10 minutes, Bitcoin adds a new block of transactions to its ledger. A block is a batch of validated transactions. Its header includes the previous block's hash, which links it to the chain. Bitcoin adjusts its mining difficulty to keep blocks about 10 minutes apart, and the miner who adds a block receives a subsidy of new bitcoin, 3.125 BTC since the 2024 halving.

slides.title: The chain
slides.body: Each block stores the previous block's hash, a unique fingerprint of its data. Change an old block, and every later link breaks.

slides.title: Agreement
slides.body: Consensus is how a network of computers agrees on the next block without a central boss. Bitcoin uses proof of work; Ethereum uses proof of stake.

slides.title: Two ways to earn the right to add a block
slides.body: In proof of work, miners spend computing power. In proof of stake, validators lock up coins as collateral. Ethereum switched to proof of stake in September 2022. That cut its energy use by about 99.95%.

slides.title: Explain it without hype
slides.body: Say a blockchain is a shared ledger whose blocks are linked by hashes. Plain, precise explanations stand out.

slides.title: The rule
slides.body: A blockchain is trusted because changing the past means redoing everything after it.
